transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

Um… I guess I’m here because I’ve just kind of stopped caring about things. I don’t mean to sound dramatic, but things I used to actually look forward to—my art classes, board-game nights, hiking… even trying to get back on the soccer team—I just can’t make myself care about any of it.

Mostly I sit in my room and let everything slip. I know that probably sounds bad… I’m trying to explain it right.
Have you been hearing voices when no one is there?

Um… yes. I mean, not all the time, and I know that sounds… bad. But sometimes I hear a woman’s voice from the corner of my room, like near my bed, saying I ruined everything and that I should stay inside.

It’s not like a vague thought, though. It sounds really clear… like someone is standing right there next to me. Does that make sense?
Have you ever heard that woman’s voice during a time when you weren’t feeling depressed or down?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, it wasn’t when I was feeling as bad as I am now.

There was this stretch before the really heavy depression set in where I could still do some normal things, like cook sometimes or answer friends’ messages. I wasn’t completely shut down yet. But I was already hearing her voice… and I also thought the hallway lights were kind of signals about me.

It went on for weeks, I think. I’m sorry, I don’t know if that’s the kind of answer you mean.
Was there ever a time when you were hearing the voice or thinking the hallway lights were sending signals, but you were not feeling depressed at all?

Um… I don’t know if I’d say I felt totally fine, exactly, but yeah, there was a stretch before the depression got really bad where I wasn’t… like, completely down all the time.

I could still cook sometimes, and I was answering friends’ messages a bit. So from the outside I probably seemed more okay. But I was already hearing the woman’s voice, and I was thinking the hallway lights were sending signals about me. That went on for weeks, I think.

Is that what you mean?
About how long have the voice and the feeling that the hallway lights were sending signals been happening in total?

Um… in total, I guess it’s been longer than I like to admit.

It started a few months after my divorce, the voice and the thing with the hallway lights… and it’s been going on since then. So, about… a year and eight months, maybe.

I know that sounds like a long time. I probably should’ve said something sooner.
Was there ever a time for at least two weeks when you were hearing the voice or thinking the hallway lights were sending signals, but you were not feeling depressed at all?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I don’t want to overstate it, but there was a period before the depression got really bad where I wasn’t feeling depressed all the time.

I could still cook here and there, and I was answering friends sometimes, so I was more functional, I guess. But the woman’s voice was already happening, and I was already thinking the hallway lights were like… signals about me.

That was for weeks, I think. So yes, probably at least two weeks. Is that the kind of thing you’re asking?
For at least six months in a row, have these experiences been happening without fully going away?

Yeah… I think so. It hasn’t really fully stopped, not for a long stretch.

It started not too long after the divorce, and it’s been… almost two years now, I guess. About a year and eleven months. There might be days where it’s less intense, so I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but it hasn’t really gone away for six months or anything like that. Is that what you mean?
Have you ever had a period where you felt unusually energized or high and needed much less sleep?

Um… I don’t think so. Not like “high” or full of energy.

I’ve had nights where I didn’t sleep much, but I wouldn’t say I needed less sleep in a good way, if that makes sense. It’s more just… being awake, not energized.

So I don’t think I’ve had that kind of period, no. Is that okay?
Have you ever had the voice or the feeling that the hallway lights were sending signals during a time when your mood felt unusually up or elevated?

No… I don’t think so. I mean, I’m trying to think, but I don’t remember ever feeling unusually up or elevated when that was happening.

If anything, it was just happening, and my mood wasn’t like… high. I don’t think I’ve had that kind of “up” period. Is that the distinction you’re asking about?
